tasks.title: Backup: daily rsync --link-dest snapshots + restore

Restore script restore_snapshot.sh <project> <date> with dry-run + y/N confirmation. Verified weekly by T-24 (alerts if 2+ days missed). kira-hq auto-commits every 10 min to GH Pages (already exists per PRD) = continuous backup complement.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration: create 8 fake snapshot dirs, run snapshot.sh, verify oldest removed. Restore dry-run prints correct plan.

tasks.title: Cron failure handling: retry + incidents + stale + /unstale
tasks.description: Implements §6.3 policy end-to-end.
tasks.details: PRD §6.3. Policy: (1) fail → retry once after 60s; (2) second fail → pipeline_log status=fail + ~/.kira-hq/incidents/<ts>-<project>.md (stderr + last 50 stdout lines); (3) Telegram alert; (4) mark project status=stale until /unstale ack; (5) stale projects skipped by cron dispatcher (prevents alert storms).
tasks.testStrategy: Integration: mocked failing skill triggers retry, then incident file, then stale mark. /unstale round-trip (wired in T-21) flips back to active.

tasks.title: kira-hq add-project CLI + skill

Skill wrapper for Hermes.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration: happy-path + each validation branch tested. Idempotent: duplicate name raises collision without partial writes.

tasks.title: Execution wrapper: provider-aware task expansion (kira-hq-execute skill)
tasks.description: Wrapper skill kira-hq-execute that detects active LLM provider and decides task granularity: parent for Sonnet/Opus, expand to subtasks for Kimi/weaker.
tasks.details: PRD §6.16. Implement ~/.kira-hq/skills-shared/kira-hq-execute/SKILL.md + scripts/kira_hq_execute.py. Behavior: (1) read task ID from CLI/cron arg; (2) detect provider via env KIRA_HQ_PROVIDER (set by Hermes per-job, default 'sonnet'); (3) lookup provider class in policy table from PRD §6.16 (opus|sonnet-4.6|haiku-4.5 -> parent, kimi-2.6|sonnet-4.5|openrouter-fallback -> subtasks); (4) if subtasks: run `task-master expand --id=N --num=auto` (idempotent — skip if subtasks already exist); (5) auto-populate subtasks from plan.md atomic steps (read corresponding plan section, emit one subtask per checkbox step preserving code blocks — NOT LLM-regenerated); (6) execute parent OR each subtask in sequence with task-master set-status transitions; (7) append pipeline.log entry per execution with new column expand_used (true|false); (8) on parent failure twice (per §6.3 retry), demote to subtask granularity for retry #3 before alerting; (9) Hermes invokes this skill instead of raw claude calls so autolearn observes provider×task-type success patterns. Update §6.1 pipeline log schema to include provider + expand_used columns (already done in PRD).
tasks.testStrategy: Smoke: kira-hq-execute --task-id=8 --provider=sonnet (parent path), kira-hq-execute --task-id=8 --provider=kimi-2.6 (subtask path with mocked task-master expand). Integration: real expand on T-8, verify subtasks contain code blocks copied from plan.md §8 (not paraphrased). E2E: full Hermes cron cycle invokes wrapper on a fixture task with provider=kimi-2.6, verify (a) subtasks materialized, (b) each executed sequentially, (c) pipeline.log entries show expand_used=true. Negative test: parent task fails 2x in a row -> retry 3 demoted to subtasks automatically.

tasks.title: Orchestrator token-efficiency playbook + clean-worktree policy
tasks.description: Write a concrete controller-efficiency proposal covering worktree hygiene, structured handoffs, artifact files, diff-first inspection, and escalation rules to cut orchestrator token burn.
tasks.details: Create a compact implementation proposal for Hermes/Kira-HQ that reduces controller token usage without losing verification quality. The write-up should: (1) define worktree-per-task or equivalent clean-tree isolation, (2) mandate structured handoff summaries from workers instead of raw logs, (3) route long test/review outputs to artifact files rather than the controller chat, (4) make diff-stat/name-only the default controller inspection path with full diffs only on exception paths, (5) classify noisy operational files (.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json, kanban_board.md, pipeline.log.md) separately from feature diffs, and (6) document when to escalate to Opus/Sonnet versus staying on cheaper workers. Include rollout order, trade-offs, and success metrics. Before implementation, send the proposal to Opus 4.7 for architecture review and record the verdict/recommended amendments.
tasks.testStrategy: Review checklist: proposal must name at least 5 concrete savings mechanisms, define one default workflow for controller handoffs, include success metrics (controller tokens/task, avg diff size inspected, artifact count, review-loop count), and capture an Opus 4.7 review verdict plus any requested amendments.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 1: machine-readable handoff contract
tasks.description: Implement the structured worker handoff schema for the orchestrator token-efficiency model.
tasks.details: Create a machine-parseable handoff contract for delegated workers. Define required fields (`task_id`, `step`, `worker`, `worktree`, `lane`, `files[]`, `tests`, `risks[]`, `artifacts[]`, `next`, `status`) and provide one canonical serializer/parser path used by controller-facing workflow code and artifacts. Update docs and examples so workers return structured summaries instead of free-form prose. This is the first implementation stage from Task 26.
tasks.testStrategy: Smoke: parser rejects malformed handoffs and accepts valid YAML/JSON examples. Integration: a delegated worker fixture emits a structured handoff and the controller-side reader parses it into a normalized object.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 1 integration check: handoff contract enforcement
tasks.description: Add integration checks proving the controller rejects invalid worker handoffs and accepts valid ones.
tasks.details: Implement integration tests for the Stage 1 handoff contract. Cover success and failure cases: missing required keys, undeclared artifacts, invalid task/lane metadata, and normalized parsing of valid handoffs. Ensure the controller fails closed when handoff structure is broken.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration: fixture handoffs covering valid and invalid cases; controller path must reject malformed payloads and accept valid payloads with deterministic normalization. Add at least one regression test asserting free-form summaries are not accepted.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 2: diff-first inspection + artifact/noise policy
tasks.description: Implement the controller fast-path that reads summary metadata first and full diffs/artifacts only on exception paths.
tasks.details: Add the Stage 2 execution policy from Task 26: default controller inspection uses `git diff --name-only` and `git diff --stat`; long logs move under a predictable artifact root; `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json`, `kanban_board.md`, and `pipeline.log.md` are classified as operational noise unless the task explicitly targets them. Wire exception triggers into the decision path and document the artifact root convention.
tasks.testStrategy: Smoke: controller fast-path returns a decision from name-only/stat input without opening full diffs. Integration: artifact-root convention is enforced, noisy operational files are excluded from default semantic review, and exception-triggered tasks open only the required deeper context.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 2 integration check: integrity check + exception triggers
tasks.description: Add integration coverage for files[] vs git diff integrity checking and concrete exception-trigger behavior.
tasks.details: Implement integration tests for the Stage 2 controller gate. The controller must compare declared `files[]` against actual git diff output, fail handoff on mismatch, and open full review only when explicit exception thresholds are hit (e.g. touched files > 8, auth/security paths, fail-loop >= 2, HIGH risk, ambiguous PRD references).
tasks.testStrategy: Integration: fixture repos or mocked git outputs proving (1) mismatched `files[]` fails closed, (2) normal tasks stay on diff-first fast-path, and (3) exception triggers escalate inspection deterministically.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 3: worktree automation + parallel lane merge-back
tasks.description: Implement ephemeral worktree-per-task execution with automatic local merge-back and cleanup.
tasks.details: Build Stage 3 from Task 26: create/adopt ephemeral local worktrees per task or parallel lane, record worktree/lane metadata in handoffs, support parallel execution lanes, merge selected lane branches back locally into the controller branch, and remove temporary branches/worktrees automatically on closeout. Remote GitHub branches remain opt-in only.
tasks.testStrategy: Smoke: create task worktree, run a narrow operation, merge back locally, and clean up branch/worktree. Integration: parallel lanes use separate worktrees, controller selects winner or merge order, merges selected lane(s) back locally, and deletes losing/temp branches.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 3 integration check: parallel lanes + cleanup
tasks.description: Add integration checks for parallel-task worktrees, lane selection, merge-back, and cleanup.
tasks.details: Implement integration tests around the worktree lifecycle. Cover lane creation, lane labeling, parallel execution isolation, local merge-back into controller branch, deletion of losing branches, and worktree cleanup after task close. Verify no default remote branch publication occurs.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration: synthetic parallel lanes produce separate worktrees and branch refs; selected winner merges back locally; losing refs are removed; worktrees are pruned. Regression: completed tasks must not leave long-lived local or remote lane branches by default.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 4: token-efficiency metrics + threshold tuning
tasks.description: Instrument the orchestrator token-efficiency metrics and tuning loop.
tasks.details: Implement Stage 4 metrics from Task 26: controller tokens per task, average file count inspected, average diff size inspected, artifact count/bytes, fail-loop count, integrity-check failure count, and exception-path rate. Add a baseline/after comparison workflow so routing thresholds can be tuned with data rather than intuition.
tasks.testStrategy: Smoke: metrics writer records all required fields for a sample task. Integration: aggregate a baseline window over prior tasks and compare it with post-rollout runs, producing a summary suitable for weekly review or dashboard consumption.

tasks.title: Controller Stage 4 integration check: end-to-end rollout validation
tasks.description: Run an end-to-end integration validation of the new orchestrator flow across all stages.
tasks.details: Implement the final integration check task for the rollout. Validate the combined flow: structured handoff -> integrity check -> diff-first inspection -> artifact routing -> worktree-per-task / parallel lanes -> merge-back cleanup -> metrics capture. This task should prove the full controller policy works together under a realistic delegated-task simulation.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration/E2E: simulate at least one normal task and one parallel-lane task, confirm the controller stays on fast-path when possible, escalates correctly on exception paths, merges back locally, cleans worktrees, and records metrics. The final report should quantify expected token savings against the pre-rollout baseline.

tasks.title: Claude-first orchestrator path + Hermes/Qwen worker bridge
tasks.description: Make local Claude Code the primary orchestrator interface while Hermes becomes an invokable CLI worker that routes routine code work through OpenRouter qwen3-coder and shares the same Kira-HQ substrate.
tasks.details: Follow-up to the dual-interface audit. Build the missing pieces needed so local Claude Code becomes the main orchestrator interface for this machine while Hermes is used as a bash-invoked worker CLI for implementation work. Requirements: (1) add repo-root CLAUDE.md describing the shared Kira-HQ system, the canonical task/tag context, and the rule that Claude is the orchestrator while Hermes is the implementation worker; (2) add neutral local CLI entrypoints so Claude can safely list/add/update tasks without hand-editing tasks.json; (3) define and document the Hermes invocation contract from Claude, including calling Hermes from bash with the OpenRouter qwen3-coder worker/model used in Hermes; (4) inspect Claude plugin/MCP/extensibility and add the missing OpenRouter/Qwen access path analogous to the existing Codex plugin/tooling so Claude can delegate routine code work to OR/qwen; (5) preserve one shared filesystem/data substrate (projects.yaml, task store, pipeline/global logs, shared skills); (6) keep Hermes-specific vs shared skills intentional and document promotion rules; (7) update docs and doctor/readiness checks so the second interface is explicit, not implicit.
tasks.testStrategy: Smoke: direct Claude-oriented local commands for task listing and task creation hit the same live store as Hermes. Integration: a Claude-side invocation path can call Hermes as a bash worker with the configured OpenRouter qwen model and record provider/pipeline metadata on the shared substrate. Verification should include symlink health, currentTag guard, and explicit proof that no manual JSON editing is needed.

tasks.title: End-to-end validation: Claude command delegates implementation to OR/Qwen via Hermes worker
tasks.description: Prove the new two-interface setup works by executing one controlled end-to-end delegation from Claude orchestrator to Hermes worker using the OpenRouter qwen implementation path.
tasks.details: After Task 35 lands, implement an end-to-end validation task that proves the architecture with a real controlled run. Scenario: Claude receives a user command in the repo context, decides to delegate routine implementation to the OR/qwen path through Hermes-as-worker, executes the delegated step, and returns a structured handoff/result while both interfaces continue to use the same task store, shared skills, and shared logs. The validation should exercise at least: task visibility parity, safe mutation path, Claude-to-Hermes bash invocation, Hermes-to-OpenRouter qwen worker routing, shared pipeline logging/metadata, and an operator-readable success report. Prefer a narrow fixture/sandboxed task rather than risky broad repo mutation.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration/E2E: run one real delegation from Claude-orchestrator to Hermes-worker to OR/qwen on a bounded fixture task; assert the delegated action occurred, shared state/logs were updated consistently, and the final result/report flowed back to Claude without breaking task parity. Include a negative/diagnostic check for misconfiguration (missing OR credentials or missing bridge command) that fails clearly.
